steps.title: Morning briefing
steps.ai: Good morning, Fiona. Before the ALCO prep, three portfolio signals need a look. The most urgent: Home Improvement Loan (unsecured) 60-day delinquency has reached 1.8%, up from 1.1% two quarters ago and now past your 1.5% aligned parameter. It is the only pool trending outside tolerance. A portfolio is also nearing a board limit, and liquidity and shutdown exposure is building. Want to start with the delinquency trend?
steps.viz: Three priority signal cards: Delinquency drift (critical), Portfolio nearing a board limit (warning), Rate and liquidity pressure (warning). KPI row beneath.
followUps: Show delinquency trends by segment
Which portfolios are near their board limits?
What is building on rates and liquidity?

steps.title: Delinquency by segment
steps.user: Show delinquency trends by loan segment, and flag any pool trending up or outside our aligned parameters.
steps.ai: Most segments are flat or improving. One is not. Home Improvement Loan (unsecured) 60-day delinquency is 1.8%, up from 1.1% two quarters ago and now above your 1.5% aligned parameter. First mortgage and HELOC are steady at 0.4% and 0.6%. The rise is concentrated in loans originated in the last 18 months, through the contractor channel. The Home Improvement Loan book is the pool to watch; everything else sits inside tolerance.
steps.viz: Delinquency-by-segment trend lines over eight quarters, the Home Improvement Loan book flagged red and crossing the 1.5% parameter line.
steps.sources: Jack Henry Symitar (loan servicing and delinquency)
followUps: Which portfolios are near their board limits?
What is driving the Home Improvement Loan rise?
Model a downside on this pool

steps.title: Portfolios against board limits
steps.user: Which portfolios are approaching our board risk-tolerance limits, such as mortgages capped at 600% of net worth?
steps.ai: One portfolio is close. First mortgage is at $655M, which is 571% of net worth against your 600% board cap, so about $33M of headroom before the limit. No other portfolio is within fifteen points of its limit. At the current pace of first-mortgage growth, you reach the cap in roughly two quarters.
steps.viz: Portfolio-versus-limit horizontal bars with headroom shaded, first mortgage nearest the 600% line, a two-quarter projection marker.
steps.sources: Symitar, Cornerstone, UST Finex (portfolio balance, capital position, risk limits)
followUps: Model a government shutdown on the portfolio
How much can we run off to stay under the cap?
Show capital and liquidity headroom

steps.title: Government-shutdown employment shock
steps.user: Model a government shutdown as an employment shock. What happens to our members and our loan portfolio?
steps.ai: Modeled on our own members' behavior, not industry averages, which matters because our field of membership is concentrated in the Senate community. In a 30-day shutdown, an estimated 18% of affected members draw down deposits and about 6% delay a loan payment. Projected 60-day delinquency rises across unsecured consumer credit, led by the Home Improvement Loan book, and modeled loan losses increase about $4.2M over two quarters. Because this is calibrated to our members, the impact lands sharper and faster than a generic ALM shock would show. This is the scenario an ALM model alone would miss.
steps.viz: Shutdown-scenario impact panel: members affected, deposit drawdown and payment-delay rates, projected delinquency by segment (Home Improvement Loan leading), and modeled loss over two quarters.
steps.sources: UST Finex (asset-liability model), Symitar (member and portfolio history)
followUps: Do we have enough capital and liquidity?
What is our shutdown playbook?
Show deposit activity by SEG

steps.title: Capital and liquidity cushion
steps.user: For that shutdown scenario, do we have enough dry powder? What happens to our capital ratios and liquidity?
steps.ai: Under the 30-day shutdown scenario your net worth ratio moves from 7.50% to about 7.2%, still well capitalized, and on-hand liquidity covers projected outflows for the quarter with roughly $35M to spare. The pressure point is deposit outflow concentrated in a few Senate-community payroll groups, which pushes loan-to-share from 84% toward the funding-review trigger. You have dry powder, but the scenario narrows it. I reconciled the capital position across the core, the ledger, and the ALM model, so the cushion is provable.
steps.viz: Capital-ratio and liquidity gauges before and after, loan-to-share crossing the funding-review trigger, and a small reconciliation panel tying the capital figure to its three sources.
steps.sources: Symitar, Cornerstone, UST Finex (capital position, liquidity, ALM)
followUps: What is our shutdown playbook?
Show deposit activity by SEG
Export this for the board

steps.title: Shutdown playbook
steps.user: For a shutdown of this kind, what is our pre-established playbook?
steps.ai: Your board playbook maps actions to a shutdown trigger by severity. At an anticipated or short shutdown: proactive outreach and hardship-deferral offers to the affected payroll groups, and a pause on Home Improvement Loan marketing to the most exposed segments. At an extended shutdown: activate the emergency-liquidity line, tighten unsecured underwriting, and stand up the member relief program the board pre-approved. Each action is pulled as written in the approved playbook, so this is a decision, not a rebuild.
steps.viz: Trigger-to-action table drawn from the board playbook, each row tied to a shutdown severity band, with the recommended action highlighted for the modeled scenario.
followUps: Show deposit activity by SEG
Draft the ALCO summary
Export the briefing for the board

steps.title: Deposit activity by SEG
steps.user: Show deposit activity by SEG group, and trigger an alert if more than a set percentage leaves.
steps.ai: Deposit activity by core SEG this month: total balances are up 0.6%, but two payroll groups are trending down. One is off 4.2% versus last month, which crosses your 3% outflow trigger, so it is flagged. The movement is mostly certificate closures chasing a competitor promotional rate rather than full attrition. Net, funding is stable, with one group to address before it compounds. I have raised the alert and attached the detail.
steps.viz: Deposit activity by SEG as bars with amount and count, the flagged group in red crossing the 3% outflow trigger, and an alert card with the attached detail.
steps.sources: Jack Henry Symitar (deposit transactions by SEG)
followUps: Draft the retention action for this SEG
Export the briefing for the board
Back to the morning signals
